item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00191","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C11","C02","C05"],"selected_candidate_label":"C11","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C11 is the President's immediately preceding letter to Secretary Lovett that the child expressly says it attaches, and it supplies both the substantive predicate and distinctive rights-based language reused in the appeal to committee chairmen. C11 explains that inadequate State action may make prompt federal legislation necessary and closes by linking servicemen's voting rights to the rights they risk their lives defending; the child converts those points into an urgent request for congressional action on the servicemen's voting bill. C02 and C05 share the attachment/transmittal and early-legislative-action structure, but neither approaches C11's direct and distinctive textual relationship.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"I am attaching for the information of your Committee copies of a letter which I wrote to Secretary of Defense Lovett, and his reply thereto, on the subject of voting by servicemen.","parent_excerpt":"Dear Mr. Lovett: Attached is a copy of my Message to Congress, March 28, 1952, on the subject of voting by servicemen","explanation":"The child expressly identifies and transmits C11 as part of the documentary basis for its congressional appeal."},{"child_excerpt":"Under these circumstances, it is even more important that the Congress take early action to enable hundreds of thousands of servicemen to vote this year.","parent_excerpt":"The extent of State action will determine whether or not it is necessary for Congress to enact Federal legislation in time to give the maximum number of servicemen the right to vote this year.","explanation":"Both use the same State-action-versus-federal-legislation mechanism and emphasize enactment in time for servicemen to vote that year."},{"child_excerpt":"those who are defending our form of Government with their lives to exercise one of the basic rights of American citizens-the right to vote","parent_excerpt":"the men and women of the armed forces will have the chance to exercise one of the great rights which they are now, in many cases, risking their lives to defend","explanation":"This is a distinctive near-verbatim rhetorical formulation linking military sacrifice, the defense of rights, and the opportunity to vote."}]}
